beats.narration_en: Why does this road stand straight up?
It's a drawbridge and Chicago has dozens of them.
Each half of the road weighs thousands of tons.
Yet two motors no stronger than a car's engine lift it in about a minute.
The secret is hidden in a pit under the street.
A counterweight heavier than the road itself hangs behind the pivot.
Like a seesaw it balances the road almost perfectly.
So the motors only have to give it a nudge.
As the road tips up the counterweight swings down into the pit.
That's why it's called a bascule, French for seesaw.
And when the next ship comes, up it goes again.
